elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause (b): "for a period of thirty (30) days following performance, the Hosting Services and Support Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner."

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause (a): "the Interface and all related software will conform in all material respects to its documentation."

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: The inserted software warranty runs only "for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery"; to reach preferred the drafter must state twelve (12) months.
Services warranty is expressed as "for a period of thirty (30) days following performance"; preferred requires ninety (90) days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "at TrueLink's option, repair or replacement of the non-conforming software or re-performance of the non-conforming Services".
"or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming software or Services."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty appears anywhere in Section 9 as rendered; the drafter would need to add an express "TrueLink will comply with all applicable laws" warranty.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious code / virus warranty is present in the rendered text; Section 9 covers only Y2K readiness plus the inserted conformance and workmanlike warranties.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: "for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, the Interface and all related software will conform in all material respects to its documentation" — 90 days, documentation conformance, Vendor-given.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: "for a period of thirty (30) days following performance, the Hosting Services and Support Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner" — meets the 30-day floor.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "Client's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at TrueLink's option, repair or replacement of the non-conforming software or re-performance of the non-conforming Services".
"or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming software or Services."

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: 90-day documentation-conformance warranty for the Interface/related software, 30-day services warranty, and repair/replacement or refund remedy all appear in operative language, not merely in the comment.

Preferred is not reached: periods are 90 days/30 days rather than 12 months/90 days, and there is no compliance-with-laws warranty and no malicious-code warranty. To move to preferred, extend the software period to twelve (12) months, extend the services period to ninety (90) days, and add express compliance-with-applicable-laws and no-malicious-code warranties.

Minimal: the redline is a single inserted paragraph adjacent to the existing Section 9 warranty; nothing is deleted or paraphrased, the favourable Y2K warranty and Vendor-cost repair language are retained, and no survival tail, at-own-expense wording, notice procedure, or other extra requirement is added. The re-performance option is inherent to the services remedy and tracks the model language rather than adding a new obligation.

Preserves intent: the disclaimer is prefaced "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT," so it does not swallow the new express warranty; the inserted clause uses only defined terms (Interface, Hosting Services, Support Services, Client, TrueLink) and creates no dangling cross-reference or contradictory retained sentence.
Drafting nit only (not a defect): "this warranty" in the remedy sentence refers to both limbs (a) and (b); consider "the warranties in this paragraph" for clarity.
